title: Count-preserving prefix banks span historical means and can produce negative slopes
statement: On three 30,000-token historical samples, synthetic bijections preserving every type’s frequency and length generate fixed-prefix scores near historical means for some length groups. A frequency-ranked prefix bank also produces negative frequency slopes in all 15 book-by-length groups, generally much steeper than the historical slopes. These fitted controls show that the metric and slope sign alone are not language-specific; they are not independent random books or a test on the manuscript.
check: Freeze the metric, sample, independent books and structured procedures before another evaluation. Test banks trained without access to target frequency tables, size and smoothing sensitivity, multiple latent processes and cipher models; report uncertainty at the work level, preserve bounded words and establish power and false-positive rates. Obtain the authors’ original implementation if possible, and implement a reviewed declarative primitive before pre-registering any manuscript claim. Do not interpret a nonzero score, a negative slope, or a match of means as evidence for language.
metric: For a sample of N tokens, word type w with frequency c(w), and token count C2(w) of all words beginning with the same first two normalized characters, define log2((N-c(w)+1)/(C2(w)-c(w)+1)). Compute the type-weighted mean and ordinary least squares slope against log2(c(w)/N) separately for lengths 4–8, requiring at least 100 types in each length group. Raw normalized Latin alphabet characters are used; no end marker is inserted. The add-one formula is an explicitly chosen competitor fraction, not the published authors’ implementation.
hand_validation: On the prefix tree cat:2, cats:1, dog:1 (N=4), C2=3,3,1 and scores are log2(3/2)=0.5849625007, log2(4/3)=0.4150374993, and log2(4)=2.0 respectively. The independent direct calculation agrees with the parent pilot; the cat prefix-of-another case retains cats as a competitor.
sampling: Use first 30,000 normalized tokens of pinned Dante, Libro de Buen Amor and Paston Letters, verifying each SHA-256. These are three distinct works but were used in earlier related exploratory analyses and are not fresh confirmation. A source sample is transformed in full, preserving token sequence, every word length and the entire type-frequency multiset. Words shorter than four characters stay unchanged; their prefixes still contribute to all C2 counts. Every transformed type of length at least four is mapped injectively to an artificial ASCII spelling with the same length, and its occurrences use the same replacement.
generators: Seed a bank of 16 or 64 distinct two-character prefixes, then independently draw a prefix uniformly for each source type and complete it with random characters, rejecting spelling collisions. Repeat three seeds 4001–4003; add an alternative 16-prefix Zipf-weighted draw. After inspecting those outputs, add 96 and 128 uniform prefixes on the same samples and seeds. Finally sort source types of length at least four by descending observed frequency and assign contiguous equal-size rank groups to 96 or 128 random prefixes, completing unique random suffixes. The latter explicitly builds frequency-conditioned prefix clusters, so negative slopes are expected and the construction is an adversarial diagnostic, not evidence of a plausible historical process. It and the larger banks were added after observing the initial results.
limitations: Synthetic lexicons are fitted to each source’s own complete counts and length distribution; short words and the token-order pattern remain from the source. Uniform bank size strongly controls score means, and frequency-ranked assignments deliberately induce slope; no blindness, independent generator calibration, bootstrap, trained decoder or meaningful generation has been shown. Slopes are substantially more negative than the source and are not quantitatively matched. The three works are not independent manuscript witnesses and are too few to estimate general performance. No manuscript or season-heldout pages were measured.
